label: Opening Hook
text: Damascus steel blades were famed for their watery patterns and sharpness, and in 2006 scientists found carbon nanotubes inside one.
title: File:Damascus steel hunting knife (4121912077).jpg

label: Terrain & Scale
text: Made from wootz crucible steel produced in South India and Sri Lanka Recognisable by flowing water-like (damask) surface patterns A 2006 Nature paper (Reibold et al.) reported carbon nanotubes and cementite nanowires in a 17th-century Damascus sabre The production method was lost around the 18th century, possibly as ores with specific trace impurities ran out Stories of blades cutting silk scarves in mid-air are legend, not documented fact
title: File:MDRF 2021- Misc Damascus Steel Dragon Blade 2 (51439188024).jpg
